title: II.6: Fugue in D minor

groocock.chapter: 9 Group 3: Fugues for Three Voices, with Stretto

entries.notes: real; overlaps the final note of the subject
incomplete: first half of inverted subject (second beat)
incomplete, including chromatic steps (fourth beat); same voice as previous inverted entry
a fifth higher, on second beat; virtually complete, with CS in bass
a beat later, a twelfth lower
incomplete: first half bar; CS in bass bar 26

episodes.material: originates from second half of bar 7: end of subject, end of CS and "free part" in triple interchangeable counterpoint, interchanged every half bar
arises from sequential extension; basically interchange of episode 1 material

18-21 three-part imitation of the beginning of the direct or inverted subject with inverted leaping quavers of bar 3; 21-24 free interchange/development of ep.1; 24-25 two-part canon on the "free part" of bars 7-8
episodes.sequence: touches iv, bVII, VI without modulating

codettas.notes: inverts last four soprano notes of bar 4; middle alludes to inverted subject; needed because answer is so much in A minor

countersubjects.first: after the third beat of bar 3 (with the semiquavers)
countersubjects.notes: heard again with answer 6-7, then only with the virtually complete soprano entries at 14 and 25 (bass, 26); unaltered with subject entry (p.15)

subject.ends: presumably first note of bar 3, overlapped by the answer
subject.notes: never appears complete after the exposition

key_plan: Review table: Exp S S S (i v i) EP/ | Dev STR EP STR STR (i i i) | Final EP STR / (i)

claims.claim: Hardly modulates; its two perfect cadences are both in the tonic.
Rejects reading second half of bar 18 as entries in iv (contrary to some commentators); treats it as episode.
Stretto 1 "academically a poor sort of stretto" since one voice has both inverted and direct subject.
Subject combines with itself in canon at the octave or the upper fifth; same for inverted subject; direct and inverted can combine.

notes: Entry keys mostly read from the key line under the diagram; their alignment with individual entries is approximate where several entries start close together.
